problem: Must every Agent be a microservice, and where is the real scaling bottleneck?
principle: Choose process boundaries from isolation, resources and independent scaling, not role names. Estimate arrival rate, fanout, mean service time and quotas, then validate under measured load/failure.
check: Can p95 replace mean service time in Little’s law?
answer: No. Mean relationships require means and assumptions; tail goals need separate validation.
diagram_title: Deployment boundaries, capacity, isolation and technology choice
scope: Design reference and local contracts; no model training or measured collaboration uplift.

procedures.state: Contracts, shared resources and failure domain.
procedures.failure: Logical Agents need not be OS processes.
procedures.case: Research and writing can begin as separate work units in one process.

procedures.state: Slots, backlog, quotas, memory and tenant limits.
procedures.failure: More workers cannot exceed an external quota.
procedures.case: CPU parsing and remote model calls need different pool policies.

procedures.state: History, worker versions, stores and availability.
procedures.failure: Platforms do not replace business authorization or idempotency.
procedures.measure: Outage, migration, recovery time and unit task cost.
procedures.case: Use mean time for capacity; test tail latency and bursts separately.
